RO_0_and_RO1.CO1_RO1_relation: NOT one statement: CO1 excludes only T_id (adjunction activity); RO1 excludes only RO-0 (record activity of occurring adjunctions). Independent axes of the same A13R0 template type; a model can satisfy CO1 with RO-0 (active but coherent) or vacuously satisfy RO1 under T_id. Both are kept.
RO_0_and_RO1.RO1: a distinction event whose parent set includes a lineage object with an unresolved incidence frontier acts nontrivially (as an A10 prefix record) on that frontier
RO_0_and_RO1.RO_0_excluded_by_source: NO - no source statement forces records (CD1I derives record REPRESENTATIONS, not record occurrence; R30 frozen)

RO_A.consistency_note: RO-D does not contradict the append: the recording event acts on PREVIOUSLY appended letters of other lineages; its own new letter remains the J_D-invariant append.
RO_A.witness: CD1I SPEC Sec 5 (lines 203-225): the unresolved append J_D is the UNIQUE local-C3-invariant isometry appending the uniform |u>, with 'no retained distinction among the new three incidence roles' as a frozen uniqueness condition. An A10 record is the write |w>|0> -> |w>|pi_l(w)> (Sec 9, lines 406-414), which retains distinction. An adjunction acting as a record on the lineage it extends would retain distinction among its own new roles, contradicting the frozen uniqueness of J_D. RO-A is closed.

RO_D.a10_compatibility: the induced act is exactly the frozen A10 form |w>|0> -> |w>|pi_l(w)>; deeper stable records append rather than rewrite (CD1I Sec 9 functoriality conditions)
RO_D.assignment: ell(lambda, e) = the maximal ancestry position k such that lambda's member x_k lies in the closed ancestry of a parent of e (maximal supported scope). The recorded act is the A10 prefix write pi_ell on lambda's frontier word.

certificates_D_le_3.multi_touch_resolution: when both parents of e touch lambda at distinct positions, the maximal position is the unique assignment satisfying the scope lemma upper bound and completeness (any smaller ell under-records a structurally supported position); no free parameter remains
certificates_D_le_3.no_over_recording: 0 failures: the (ell+1) frame's NEW member is never inside the event's scope (by maximality), so recording deeper than ell is never licensed
certificates_D_le_3.reflection_cyclic_gauge: the assignment uses only unoriented ancestry positions and role-free scope containment; it is manifestly independent of cyclic origin labels and reflection (no gauge symbol appears in the rule)
certificates_D_le_3.scope_lemma: 0 failures: every frame at positions <= ell lies inside the closed ancestry of the touching parent (frame members are ancestors), so the prefix copy distinguishes nothing the event does not structurally contain

classification.RO_X_status: remains the status quo fallback; not selected; it is the only candidate compatible with rejecting both CO1 and RO1, and keeps OD0 an externally controlled cocycle
classification.hostile_compliance: no ell tuning against N/S restriction; no A12 counts or service outcomes used to pick the record rule; no external query alphabet imported (the cylinder algebra is CD1I-native)

setting_component.answer: ONLY_THE_QUERY. The full control is gamma=(q_A,q_B,n,m) with settings in Z_9 (R28: 8x8x9x9=5184). The event determines the recorded prefix and hence the cylinder-algebra query component (at the registered depth-1 instance these are the eight source-declared local queries per factor); no structural datum of the event determines an odometer residue.
setting_component.question: does the downstream event determine the clock setting (odometer residue) of the full control, or only the query?
setting_component.residual_classification: FORCED_BY_STATE_GIVEN_A13R, not free: the lineage's inherited direct-limit clock residue (A13R; advanced per A13R0 by serviced vacuum events) is state data supplying the setting; the residual is a function of the global state, not a new premise and not an event datum

exact_certificates_D_le_3.assignment_rule: ell(lambda,e) = max ancestry position of any lineage member inside closed_anc of a parent of e (maximal supported scope)
